fields.meta_description: Describe your spending limits. Emergent builds purchase order automation that turns a request into an approved, numbered PO. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build Purchase Order Automation From Request to Receipt
fields.hero_description: Tell Emergent who can spend how much, and with which suppliers. It builds the app that turns each request into a numbered PO and tracks what arrives against it.
fields.features_subheading: Purchase order automation takes a request past its approvers to the supplier, then checks what arrives, with each sign-off logged.
fields.feature_1:
Purchase requests with a budget check

Staff enter the item, supplier, quantity and cost center on one form. Each request is checked against what that cost center has left this quarter before it reaches an approver.
fields.feature_2:
Approval limits by amount and category

Requests route by dollar amount and category. IT hardware adds the IT lead, anything over your limit adds finance, and a reminder chases any approver silent for two days.
fields.feature_3:
Numbered POs sent to the supplier

When the last approver signs, the app assigns the next PO number, fills your PO template with terms and the ship-to address, and emails the PDF to the supplier's order contact.
fields.feature_4:
Receiving from a phone at the dock

Whoever unpacks a delivery records what arrived against each PO line. A short shipment keeps the balance on order, and a damaged carton is logged with a photo for the buyer.
fields.feature_5:
Matching when the invoice lands

Supplier invoices are read into fields and compared with the PO and its receipts. Lines that agree go on to payables. A price or quantity gap waits for the buyer who ordered it.
fields.feature_6:
Your purchasing rules, exported to GitHub

Approval limits and numbering rules export to your GitHub on paid plans as readable code. Every requisition and PO, with its receipts, is a row in a database your team owns.

fields.tab_content_1:
Six desks become PO-2291 after two sign-offs

Marta Ruiz in facilities asks for six standing desks at $810 each, $4,860 in all. Any request over $2,500 needs the department head and then finance. Leo Grant approves first, and Hana Ito, the controller, approves from Slack. PO-2291 then goes to Northwind Office Supply as a PDF and joins the open PO list.
fields.tab_content_2:
Low stock drafts its own PO for the buyer to send

Each night the app reads stock counts from the inventory sheet and compares every item with its reorder point. Nitrile gloves are down to 38 boxes against a reorder point of 60. A draft PO for 200 boxes from Globex Medical at $6.50 a box goes to Dana Cole for review before it is sent.
fields.tab_content_3:
Receiving a short delivery keeps the rest on order

At the dock, Sam Okafor opens PO-2276 on a phone and counts 40 of the 60 cartons of exam-table paper. The receipt posts for 40, and the PO stays open for the other 20. Dana Cole gets a note to confirm the backorder date, and Globex Medical's invoice is matched against the 40 that arrived.
fields.tab_content_4:
The owner hears once a blanket PO is over 80% used

Brightline Clinics signed a $24,000 blanket PO with Acme Facility Services for a year of cleaning. Every monthly invoice is drawn against PO-2150. When October's $2,500 invoice takes the total drawn to $20,000, over 80% used, Owen Price, the operations manager, gets a direct message showing $4,000 left.

fields.howto_description: Steps one to three are policy decisions your finance and operations leads make on paper. The rest turn them into a working app, tested on real requests before anyone relies on it.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with your purchasing policy as it is written, then note where people work around it. Who can buy without a PO, which categories need IT or legal, and which suppliers are preferred. Those answers become the first rules Emergent builds.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Give each limit a dollar figure and a named role: department heads up to $2,500, finance above it, the CFO above $25,000. Add the exceptions, such as software that always needs IT whatever it costs. Describe them in plain sentences.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick a numbering format before go-live, since suppliers quote it back on every invoice. A prefix and a running number, like PO-2291, is enough for most teams. Decide too which fields print on the PDF: terms, ship-to address, and the buyer's contact.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Connect the accounting system your team closes in, such as QuickBooks or NetSuite. Suppliers and cost centers sync in first. Approved POs then sync back to the ledger, and each budget check reads the spend already recorded there.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name who confirms each delivery: the dock lead for goods, the requester for services. Receipts entered from a phone keep the count honest. For any invoice to be matched against the PO, a receipt has to exist first.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run last month's requisitions through the app before launch and compare each approval route with what happened by hand. Where a request went to the wrong approver, correct the rule by prompting and replay the batch until every route agrees.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Turn it on for a single department, such as facilities, for one month. Watch how long requests wait for each approver on the dashboard. Once the limits hold, add the next team and retire the shared purchasing inbox.

claims_to_source: The four common types of purchase order are standard, planned, blanket and contract
A blanket purchase order covers repeated purchases from one supplier over a set period up to an agreed limit, with releases or invoices drawn against it
A purchase requisition is an internal request to buy; the purchase order is the document sent to the supplier
Three-way matching checks the invoice against the purchase order and the receiving record; two-way matching checks the invoice against the PO only
A reorder point is the stock level at which a new order should be placed
A partial receipt leaves the remaining quantity on the purchase order open
